solutions.name: Incumbent enterprise platform
solutions.observed_positioning: Trusted by buyers, but expensive and slow to implement.

solutions.name: Internal build
solutions.observed_positioning: Fits local process, but competes with engineering priorities.

solutions.name: Consulting or agency service
solutions.observed_positioning: High-touch expertise, but margins and scale are limited.

solutions.name: Open-source project
solutions.observed_positioning: Low software cost, but support and reliability vary.

solutions.name: AI wrapper
solutions.observed_positioning: Fast to build, but easy to copy if workflow depth is missing.

solutions.name: Marketplace or network
solutions.observed_positioning: Useful when liquidity exists, hard to start from zero.

solutions.name: Mobile-first app
solutions.observed_positioning: Good distribution surface, often too shallow for serious workflows.

solutions.name: No-code automation
solutions.observed_positioning: Good for prototypes, brittle for core operations.

solutions.name: Legacy desktop software
solutions.category: Installed tool or old vertical app
solutions.observed_positioning: Embedded in workflows, poor UX and integrations.

solutions.name: Data dashboard
solutions.observed_positioning: Makes status visible, but may not drive action.

solutions.name: Community and content
solutions.observed_positioning: Can validate demand, but may not be software defensible.

solutions.name: API infrastructure
solutions.observed_positioning: Scales well if developers are the buyer, indirect otherwise.

solutions.name: Status quo
solutions.observed_positioning: Always a competitor when pain is tolerable or budget is unclear.

Use live LLM mode or add external research artifacts for named competitors.

gaps.title: Narrow painful workflow
gaps.pain: The idea needs one urgent job-to-be-done, not a broad feature set.
gaps.why_now: AI and modern software can compress expert work, but only if the workflow is specific.
gaps.evidence_needed: Interview 5 target users and capture the exact task they already spend time or money on.
gaps.risk: If the workflow is vague, the product becomes a solution looking for a problem.

gaps.title: Buyer-visible outcome
gaps.pain: Users may like the product, but the buyer needs a measurable business result.
gaps.why_now: Founders can now instrument usage, cost, and time saved from the first prototype.
gaps.evidence_needed: Ask who owns the budget and what metric would justify payment this month.
gaps.risk: Without a buyer metric, adoption can stall at free-user enthusiasm.

gaps.title: Distribution wedge
gaps.pain: A useful product still fails if reaching users is too slow or expensive.
gaps.why_now: Communities, outbound, integrations, and content can reveal a repeatable first channel.
gaps.evidence_needed: Run 3 small acquisition tests and measure replies, demos, or waitlist conversion.
gaps.risk: A channel that works once may not repeat without founder-led effort.

gaps.title: Trust and switching friction
gaps.pain: Users keep existing tools unless the new workflow is clearly safer, faster, or cheaper.
gaps.why_now: Agentic workflows can generate strong first drafts, but users need proof and control.
gaps.evidence_needed: Ask users what would make them trust the product with a real task.
gaps.risk: Trust gaps can turn an impressive demo into a non-critical side tool.

gaps.title: Defensible workflow data
gaps.pain: A generic AI interface is easy to copy unless usage creates proprietary process insight.
gaps.why_now: Every interaction can teach the system where users hesitate, correct, or approve.
gaps.evidence_needed: Define what unique data the product captures after 30 days of usage.
gaps.risk: If no proprietary learning loop exists, incumbents can clone the surface area.

personas.lens: Daily workflow pain, speed, usability, trust. Would I use this weekly?
personas.success_metric: The product saves meaningful time or reduces a real stress in a repeated task.
personas.default_objection: This sounds useful, but I already have a workaround that's good enough.

personas.lens: Budget ownership, ROI timeline, procurement friction, urgency, approval chain.
personas.success_metric: The product clearly pays for itself this quarter or protects a critical metric I own.
personas.default_objection: Who approves this purchase and why would they prioritize it over other line items?

personas.lens: Integration complexity, change management, support load, reliability, rollout risk.
personas.success_metric: The workflow fits existing operations without creating extra coordination cost.
personas.default_objection: This adds another tool my team has to learn, maintain, and debug.

personas.lens: How does the status quo, a free tool, or a large vendor defend the account?
personas.success_metric: The startup has a wedge incumbents cannot or choose not to copy quickly.
personas.default_objection: We can add this feature in one sprint, or bundle it with our existing platform.

personas.lens: Market size (must be >$50M SAM in 5 years), founder insight, venture scale path.
personas.success_metric: The idea has a sharp initial wedge and a defensible path to $10M ARR.
personas.default_objection: This is a feature, not a company. Or the market is too small for VC returns.

personas.lens: Data access, model quality, COGS, failure modes, defensibility, learning loop.
personas.success_metric: The system can be built cheaply, reliably, and improves with usage data.
personas.default_objection: The demo works, but production edge cases and data access will break it.

personas.lens: Cash flow, distrust of digital tools, WhatsApp-first workflow, no credit card. Peru 70% informal — will they pay via Yape/Plin? Will they trust a bot?
personas.success_metric: The product solves a real cost or risk I cannot solve with WhatsApp + Excel today.
personas.default_objection: ¿Por qué voy a pagar por esto si ya lo hago en WhatsApp o en papel?

personas.role: Peru institutional / public buyer (government or university)
personas.lens: UGEL/OSCE procurement cycles (6-18 months), zero discretionary budget, MINEDU/PRODUCE approval required. Public institutions in Peru cannot swipe a card.
personas.success_metric: The product fits within an existing budget code and avoids a new procurement process.
personas.default_objection: El presupuesto está comprometido. Necesita aprobación de la UGEL / PRODUCE / Rectorado.

personas.role: Peruvian Series A investor (local VC or family office)
personas.lens: Peru VC is thin (<3% of LATAM). Checks max $300K locally. Must see path to international co-investor for Series A ($500K+). Prefers ideas with LATAM expansion built into the model from day 1.
personas.success_metric: The idea can reach $1M ARR in Peru and attract a Magma/Wayra/international co-investor.
personas.default_objection: El mercado peruano solo no alcanza. ¿Cómo escala a Colombia o México en 18 meses?

personas.role: AI adoption skeptic (conservative professional in Peru)
personas.lens: Low AI adoption in Peru (5-15%). Most professionals still on Excel/Word. Distrust of AI outputs for high-stakes decisions (legal, medical, financial).
personas.success_metric: The AI outputs are accurate, explainable, and I can verify them before acting.
personas.default_objection: No voy a confiar en una IA para algo tan importante. ¿Quién responde si se equivoca?

### Simulation Consensus
- Strongest signal: Proceed only if target users describe a recent, repeated, expensive problem in their own words.
- Weakest assumption: Simulation scores are LLM estimates; live interviews must confirm.
- Adoption path: Start with a narrow concierge workflow, then productize the repeated steps.
- Pricing test: Ask for a small paid pilot tied to the buyer's success metric.
- Decision pressure: GO_WITH_CONSTRAINTS

### Recommended Interventions
- Narrow the customer segment until the end user and buyer are obvious.
- Run interviews around recent behavior, not opinions about the idea.
- Prototype the outcome manually before building a scalable product.
- Track what data or workflow insight compounds with each use.

## Kill Criteria
- Users cannot recall a recent painful instance.
- No budget owner or urgent operational metric identified.
- Workflow only mildly better than current workaround.
